artifacts.summary: Maps tram tracks running along streets. Where rails are set into the road surface they are a well-known hazard for people cycling, so this indicator serves primarily as a hazard map.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s tram track sections. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = 0.17. 4 hot-spot and 3 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of tram track sections density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 15 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over tram track sections density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do tram track sections track where people live? Tram track sections per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its tram track sections per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Tram track sections per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of tram track sections per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Coverage on foot
artifacts.summary: About 37% of the area is within 300 m on foot of a tram track section. About 62% of residents are within reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Underserved areas
artifacts.summary: Share of each neighbourhood beyond 300 m on foot of any tram track section. About 18,895 residents live beyond that reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by the fraction of its area that lies **beyond reach** (on foot) of any feature — the complement of the coverage map. Darker = more underserved. Use it to target where new provision would reach the most currently-unserved people.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Most underserved sub-areas

artifacts.description:

artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many tram track sections fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

artifacts.name: Tram track sections density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of tram track sections (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of tram track sections: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest tram track section
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest tram track section from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest tram track section. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each tram track section was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 1 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: tram_tracks · reachability: straight-line distance.
